title: Standing Authorizations for Medicaid Patient Pay — Resident Trust Fund Accounts
content:
## Policy

A standing authorization for Medicaid patient pay is honored by a transfer for the patient pay charge of the latest service month on the resident's Medical Assistance case (of two charges for the same month, the one recorded first), posted on the charge's due day or, where the account lacks the available funds that day, on the first day the funds are available.

This applies to a Resident Trust Fund Accounts account whose standing authorization, signed by the resident or legal representative, names Medicaid patient pay. The Medical Assistance case and its patient pay charges are those of the resident under Medical Assistance Nursing Facility Coverage. The standing authorization covers the patient pay bill every month without a new request.

## Business effect

The transfer is one bill transfer entry on the resident funds account. It names the patient pay charge it pays and the standing authorization it relies on, is dated the day it is processed, and lowers the account balance by the amount transferred; every later account lookup shows the lower balance.

## Posting the transfer: `post_patient_pay_transfer_45809d6d`

This is an agent-side tool. It is not in the default tool list: unlock it first, then call it.

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `trust_account_id` | the resident funds account the money comes from, as shown on the account record | identifier |
| `bill_entry_id` | the one patient pay charge being paid, as shown on that charge's line in the ledger of the resident's Medical Assistance case | identifier |
| `trust_request_id` | the signed standing authorization for patient pay the transfer relies on, as shown in the account's list of signed requests | identifier |
| `amount` | the money moved to the charge | US dollars, a positive decimal number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent, no currency sign |

**Return.** A one-line confirmation of the form "Transferred <amount> USD from account <account> to patient pay charge <charge> under authorization <authorization> as entry <new entry>; new balance <balance> USD." The presence of the new entry's reference number shows that the transfer was recorded.

## Contract Q&A

**Does posting the transfer work out the amount?** No. The tool records the amount it is given, rounded half up to the cent, as a positive figure.

**Does the transfer need a new signature each month?** No; it relies on the standing authorization already on file.
